{#ed1r} Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most common cancers and the most common cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. At least 50% of patients with CRC develop metastases . The liver is the most frequent site of metastasis from CRC. Such metastatic tumors subsequently cause hepatic dysfunction and failure and eventually death. In cases of advanced CRC, a combination treatment using three cytotoxic agents, including 5-fluorouracil, oxaliplatin, and irinotecan, and two molecular-targeted agents, including bevacizumab and epidermal growth factor receptor antibody (cetuximab or panitumumab), is the standard systemic therapy worldwide [@w:w1]. These approaches have improved the response and survival rates in patients with advanced CRC. However, an effective chemotherapy regimen in patients with advanced CRC that is refractory to these standard chemotherapies has not yet been established. Although regorafenib or trifluridine/tipiracil (TAS-102) is recommended, the survival benefits of these chemotherapies lasted 6.4–9.0 months, after which several adverse effects were encountered [@w:w2].

ops.markdown: Notably, HAIC was effective in this study even though it used the same drugs that had already failed when given systemically. Consistent with this observation, some reports have shown that HAIC with the same agents is effective in patients with systemic chemotherapy-resistant CRC [@w:w17], and we have reported a similar phenomenon in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma [@w:w18]. Although the mechanism underlying this phenomenon remains unclear, it may be explained by the high concentrations of anticancer agents achieved in the liver, which can still act against resistant tumor cells. In addition, only a small fraction of the drug reaches non-tumor tissues elsewhere in the body, so drug distribution outside the liver is limited [@w:w19]. Thus, although these treatments are suitable only for patients whose disease is largely confined to the liver, they achieve high disease control rates and, consequently, a survival benefit.
